deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of a business letter in French, written by Riemann during his stay in Pisa. It is addressed to 'Messieurs Valéry à Livourne', the Livorno office of the Valéry steamship company. It is the French version of the German draft on the previous page. Its content, with deletions resolved:

- Monsieur Romagn[ier/é] & Cie of Marseille informed Riemann on 18 November 1863 that they had shipped to Livorno for him, on the steamer (most likely 'Prince Napoléon'), the consignment 'R. 3. – 1 caisse vieux livres et effets, K[ilos] 215'. That is one crate, marked R. 3, of old books and personal effects, weighing about 215 kg.
- When Riemann went to the Valéry office in Livorno on 16 November, he obtained a promise that the crate would be forwarded to him as soon as possible once it arrived. He had been expecting it in Pisa day after day.
- The crate contains effects needed by him and his family for the winter, so the delay is very unpleasant.
- He therefore repeats his request that the crate be sent to him by railway.
- The draft closes 'J'ai l'honneur...', dated 'Pise, 29 Novembre 1863', and is signed 'B. Riemann, professeur', with the address '(Via del Museo, Casa Papini, 1° piano)'.

Historical context: Riemann spent the winter of 1863–64 in Pisa for his health, with his wife Elise. Their daughter Ida was born there on 22 December 1863, which explains the urgency about winter effects for 'ma famille'.

The page sits between:
- the German draft of the same complaint, plus a draft note to the banker Angelo Alhaique in Livorno about a letter of credit from Baur of Altona (previous page);
- a Latin fragment on the attraction of an elliptic cylinder (next page, the only mathematical context nearby).

There are no derivations to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Minor French slips typical of a draft by a non-native writer. 'rétardation' should be 'retard'. 'beaucoup désagréable' should be 'très désagréable'. 'qu'elle arrivât' was corrected by Riemann himself from 'arrive'.

results.what: Draft business letter (French) to the Valéry shipping company at Livorno about a delayed crate of books and effects, Pisa, 29 Nov 1863

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a personal business letter with no mathematical content. Its only value is biographical: it documents Riemann's address in Pisa (Via del Museo, Casa Papini, first floor) and the logistics of his 1863 move. That fits the known biography (Pisa stay 1863–64, daughter born December 1863).

checkable.asserts: 11 days elapsed between Romagnier's shipment notice (18 Nov) and the letter's date (29 Nov 1863). This is consistent with the previous page's German draft saying the crate must have been in Livorno for about 'vierzehn Tage', allowing for the redrafting dates.

transcription_corrections: 'paquebot France[?] Napoléon': the image more plausibly reads 'paquebot Prince Napoléon' (a steamer name).
'Romagnier[?] &ce': reads like 'Romagni[é/er] & Cie'. The previous page's German draft has 'Romagne'.
'K: 215' is most likely 'Kil. 215', the weight of the crate in kilograms.
The inserted 'que' replaces the struck 'et j'y avais' (not 'avait'), giving 'Comme je m'étais rendu le 16 Nov. dans votre comptoir que [= et] obtenu la promesse...'.
'arrivât {+ât+}' is a duplication: Riemann corrected 'arrive' to 'arrivât' by superscript.

'La caisse contient des effets qui nous sont nécessaires, à moi et à ma famille, pour l'hiver' is the intended final sentence. The phrase 'Je répète donc maintenant...' is interleaved in the transcription out of logical order.
Signature: 'Dr' appears struck before 'B. Riemann, professeur'.
